title: Sensei code graph — schema for visual design
purpose: A designer-facing description of the code graph: what a node is, what an edge is, how containment nests, how external libraries attach, and how an edge records WHY it resolved or failed to. Field types are the live PostgreSQL types; enum values are the live vocabularies.

sourceOfTruth.note: Generated by reading the DDL and the Rust vocabularies, then cross-checking against the running database.

scale.designImplication: Four million edges is past the point where a force-directed whole-graph view is usable. Every view should be a SCOPED query — one folder, one file, one symbol's neighbourhood at depth N — not a global layout.

containment.description: Two nesting systems meet at the file. Above the file it is filesystem/ownership; below it, parent_id inside the nodes table itself.

chain.note: A product. Owns one or more repositories.
A git remote, identified by repo_key.
THE INDEXING UNIT. Self-nesting via parent_id. Every node and edge carries folder_id, so a folder is the natural scope boundary for any view.
One row per tracked source file.
Symbols, doc sections and rationale. Nests further via nodes.parent_id.

withinNodes.mechanism: nodes.parent_id, a self-referencing foreign key. NULL means top-level in its file.

node.meaning: Any structural element of the codebase — a symbol, a doc heading, or an extracted rationale comment.

fields.name: id
fields.meaning: Primary key.

fields.name: folder_id
fields.meaning: Which repo/folder this belongs to. The scoping key for every view.

fields.name: parent_id
fields.meaning: Containment parent. NULL = top-level in its file.

fields.name: kind
fields.meaning: What sort of thing this is. See enums.node_kind.

fields.name: name
fields.meaning: Identifier or heading text. This is the label to render.

fields.name: file_id
fields.meaning: The file this node is DECLARED in. NULL for two populations that have no file by definition: reference stubs not yet matched to a declaration, and external library nodes.

fields.name: fqn
fields.meaning: Fully-qualified name (SCIP/LSIF moniker model). A definition and every reference to it share one node keyed on this, which is how a call edge gets a real target instead of a name guess.

fields.name: resolved
fields.meaning: True once a declaration has been seen. False = a reference-first stub still waiting for its definition. RENDER THESE DIFFERENTLY — a false node is a known-unknown, not an error.

fields.name: language
fields.meaning: Language slug derived from the file extension.

fields.name: signature
fields.meaning: Abbreviated type signature. Good hover/tooltip content.

fields.name: description
fields.meaning: Human-readable summary.

fields.name: content
fields.meaning: Full body text — markdown for doc sections, comment text for rationale.

fields.name: docstring
fields.meaning: Extracted JSDoc/TSDoc/rustdoc.

fields.name: line_start
fields.meaning: One-based start line. Enables jump-to-source.

fields.name: line_end
fields.meaning: One-based end line. line_end - line_start is a usable size signal.

fields.name: is_exported
fields.meaning: Part of the file's public surface. A strong candidate for visual emphasis.

fields.name: is_test
fields.meaning: Belongs to a test file. Needs a first-class filter toggle — test nodes are a large fraction of any real graph.

fields.name: community_id
fields.meaning: Leiden cluster id, batch-computed. NULL until computed. This is the natural grouping/colouring key for a cluster view.

fields.name: embedding
fields.meaning: Semantic embedding, HNSW-indexed. Powers 'find similar' and semantic search, not layout.

fields.name: tags
fields.meaning: Free filtering tags.

fields.name: props
fields.meaning: Per-kind extras. Section: {level:2}. Rationale: {tag:'WHY'}. Directory module: {dir:'...'}.

fields.name: modified_at
fields.meaning: Last write.

populations.description: Three visually distinct populations share this table. Conflating them is the most common way a code-graph view misleads.

kinds.name: declaration
kinds.meaning: Real code that was read. Has a location.

kinds.name: referenceStub
kinds.test: file_id IS NULL AND resolved = false
kinds.meaning: Something referenced but never found. A known gap — show it, dimmed; never drop it.

kinds.name: external
kinds.meaning: A third-party symbol. resolved = true, because the external symbol IS the definition. Belongs visually outside the repo boundary.

edge.meaning: A typed relationship between two nodes.

fields.name: id
fields.meaning: Primary key.

fields.name: folder_id
fields.meaning: Scoping key.

fields.name: source_id
fields.meaning: The node the relationship starts at. Always resolved.

fields.name: target_id
fields.meaning: The node it points at. NULL when the target could not be placed.

fields.name: target_name
fields.meaning: The name that was written at the use site. Carries an unresolved edge's meaning when target_id is NULL.

fields.name: target_file
fields.meaning: Best-known file for an unresolved target.

fields.name: kind
fields.meaning: Relationship type. See enums.edge_kind.

fields.name: confidence
fields.meaning: How the edge was obtained. See enums.edge_confidence.

fields.name: confidence_score
fields.meaning: 0.00-1.00, used by similarity and duplicate edges. Good for line weight/opacity on those kinds only.

fields.name: props
fields.meaning: Extras, MERGED on re-insert so a later writer cannot erase an earlier one. imports: {names:[...]}. duplicates: {similarity:0.86}. extends/implements: {relation:'extends'|'implements'|'trait_impl'}. Also holds props.occurrences — see occurrences below.

fields.name: resolved_via
fields.meaning: WHY this edge was placed. One of enums.resolved_via. NULL on a missed edge.

fields.name: unresolved_reason
fields.meaning: WHY this edge was not placed. One of enums.unresolved_reason. NULL on a placed edge.

fields.name: modified_at
fields.meaning: Last write.

edge.verdictInvariant: Exactly one of resolved_via / unresolved_reason is set on any edge. BOTH NULL means the writer recorded no verdict — the pre-v2 shape — and is itself a category worth showing rather than hiding.

occurrences.location: props.occurrences, an object KEYED BY FILE PATH
occurrences.meaning: One edge aggregates many use sites. Each entry carries that use site's own span and its own {rung, reason}. The edge-level resolved_via/unresolved_reason are the REDUCTION over this list.
occurrences.designImplication: An edge is not one arrow — it is a bundle. A detail panel can legitimately show 'called from 7 sites across 3 files', each with its own outcome.

edge.deploymentStatus: resolved_via and unresolved_reason are defined in the DDL but are NOT YET present in the running database (verified 2026-09-28: the live sensei.edges has 11 columns and neither of these). Any mock data for these two fields is design-ahead, not live-backed.

tables.libraries: The library itself: name, kind, ecosystem, description, homepage_url, repository_url, icons, embedding.
tables.library_versions: Per-version rows: version, resolved_version, source_type, docs_url, page_count, is_latest.
tables.library_packages: The package names a library is published under (one library can have several).
tables.referenced_libraries: The JOIN that matters for the graph: folder_id -> library_id, with version_used. This is how a repo attaches to its dependencies.

library.meaning: External dependencies, held separately from code nodes. A library is reached from a folder through referenced_libraries, and individual external SYMBOLS appear in the nodes table as 'lib·'-prefixed nodes.
library.designImplication: There are two distinct external representations and they answer different questions: referenced_libraries answers 'what does this repo depend on' (1,904 libraries), while lib· nodes answer 'which external symbol does this call reach'. A dependency panel wants the first; an edge target wants the second.

values.meaning: A callable invokes another callable.
A type implements an interface or trait. props.relation distinguishes a Rust trait impl from Java-style implementation.
A type extends another.
A file imports from a file or module. props.names lists the imported bindings.
Module-level dependency.
Documentation traces to a code symbol.
A doc section references a symbol or file.
A doc file covers a source file.
A comment explains a symbol.
Structurally identical code. confidence_score = similarity.
Semantically similar, inferred from embeddings.
Read from the syntax tree. Certain.
Derived from embeddings or BM25. Probable.
Drift or a gap. Uncertain.

resolved_via.description: WHY a placed edge was placed — a LADDER, strongest evidence first. The order is the strength order and is meaningful: it says how much the graph should be trusted on this edge.

values.meaning: The file declares the target itself.
An import in scope binds the head of the path.
The file's own text names the target — it declares the type, or imports it by a package-rooted path.
A type in this scan declares the target as its member, in another file.
A glob import covers the target's module. The name was never written down — the weakest first-party rung.
A path rooted at this package, needing no import.
A fully-qualified path into a third party.
The language prelude supplies it.

unresolved_reason.description: WHY an edge could not be placed. NOT an error list — most of these are correct outcomes, and the design should not render them as failures.

values.meaning: The walk does not yet handle this syntactic shape.
The receiver has no declared type to resolve against.
The receiver's type could not be determined.
Nothing in scope binds the name.
Several candidates matched and none dominates. Resolving anyway would be confidently wrong.
The target is chosen at runtime. Not knowable statically.
The call is generated by a macro.
Framework/generated glue rather than authored intent.
The target is outside the scanned source. Correct, not missing.
No verdict recorded by the writer.

renderingRules.rule: An unresolved edge is dimmed, never dropped.
renderingRules.why: The edge is real; only its endpoint is unplaceable. Dropping it makes the graph look more complete than it is, which is the single most misleading thing this visualisation can do. 'external_boundary' in particular is a correct outcome, not a defect.

renderingRules.rule: Scope every view. Never attempt a global layout.
renderingRules.why: 4,077,549 edges. Views must be rooted at a folder, a file, or a symbol with a depth limit.

renderingRules.rule: Give is_test its own filter, on by default or off by default but always visible.
renderingRules.why: Test nodes are a large share of any repo and swamp production structure when mixed in.

renderingRules.rule: Separate the three node populations visually.
renderingRules.why: A declaration, an unresolved reference stub, and an external lib· symbol look identical if you only read `name`, but they mean very different things about how much the graph knows.

renderingRules.rule: Use resolved_via rank as a trust signal, not just a label.
renderingRules.why: The ladder is ordered. An edge placed by 'declared_here' is a fact; one placed by 'through_a_glob' is the weakest first-party inference and deserves to look less certain.

renderingRules.rule: Treat an edge as a bundle of occurrences.
renderingRules.why: props.occurrences is keyed by file and each use site carries its own span and outcome, so a detail view can show where a relationship actually happens.

openQuestionsForDesign: Schema entities (database tables/columns as graph nodes) are specified but not yet built — see docs/spec/indexer/20-schema-entities.md. If the design should accommodate them, a column is a Field node under a Struct/table parent, and a foreign key is a `references` edge.
community_id is NULL until the Leiden pass runs, so a cluster view needs an empty state.
resolved_via / unresolved_reason are not yet in the live database; designs using them are ahead of the data.
